messages:
incident-bot: PAGE - High 5xx and request latency observed for inference.prod (kv-cache miss spike). Severity: P1. Current customers affected: some long-tail dedicated customers and a 5% error spike for hosted API. Alert link: https://ops.internal/alerts/INC-1812345678 :rotating_light:

maria: I'm on it. seeing the same in SLO dashboard — latency p95 jumped from 120ms -> 980ms starting ~10:12 UTC. KV cache hit-rate dropped from 98% -> 62% around same time.

sachin: grabbing logs. Can someone post the query that shows the hit-rate timeline?

evans: used this query already: https://logs.internal/query?q=service%3Akv-cache+env%3Aprod+metric%3AKV_HIT_RATE&from=10:00&to=10:30

leah: quick note: we shipped a small cache key normalization change in commit a3f4b2 ~09:58 UTC (rollout to 30%). Could be related. See PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/428

maria: good catch. I'm going to pause rollouts for that PR and check canary buckets.

maria: sharing sample log lines (one-liner redacted) ->
```
ts=2026-03-14T10:12:21Z service=kv-cache prefix=emb:embed-v2 key=emb:12345 action=MISS reason=prefix_mismatch ttl=0 shard=5
ts=2026-03-14T10:12:21Z service=kv-cache prefix=emb:embed-v2 key=emb:23456 action=MISS reason=evicted_by_reaper ttl=0 shard=2
```

sachin: That first reason "prefix_mismatch" looks suspicious. Could be normalization change splintering prefixes (old prefix=emb-v1, new=emb:embed-v2).

evans: I pulled request diff — they replaced '-' with ':' in prefix construction. If some services still write with old format, cache warming will miss.

maria: Hypothesis 1: rollout normalization causing widespread prefix mismatch -> sudden cache miss storm -> backend requests spike -> higher latency and 5xx.
leah: Hypothesis 2: reaper/eviction TTL policy was accidentally lowered in same release window (I see an infra config bump in the same PR). That would explain "evicted_by_reaper" lines.

product-ops: Customer-impact snapshot (10:12-10:30): ~12 customers saw >=3x latency; hosted API 5xx rate delta +4.8% over baseline; billing-sensitive tenants impacted. Need comms if sustained.

maria: Immediate mitigations I started:
- paused PR rollout (stopped canary)
- increased kv-cache capacity by +20% (scaled nodes)
- temporarily relaxed reaper eviction threshold to previous value (rolled config back)
- enabled routing fallback: requests for models with emb prefix go to fallback shard if miss > threshold

deploy-bot: Rollout pause acknowledged for PR a3f4b2. Eviction config rollback deployed to kv-configs@10:23 UTC by deploy-bot.

evans: After scale + eviction rollback — hit-rate climbed from 62% -> 89% by 10:28, p95 latency back down to ~140ms. 5xx dropped to baseline. Looks like mitigation worked.

sachin: Captured timeline notes for RCA: 09:58 commit shipped -> 10:12 hit-rate drop start -> 10:18 mitigation (scale + eviction rollback start) -> 10:28 partial recovery -> 10:36 full recovery. I'm saving logs to: https://logs.internal/saves/1812345678-kv-incident

maria: Quick check: are there any long-tail keys that never warmed? We should run a rewarm job for old prefix -> new prefix mapping so misses don't persist. Planning a one-off rewarm for high-traffic keys.

leah: I'm going to open a rewarm job ticket and link it here. Rewarm ticket: https://issues.internal/RED-7892 (reindex/rewarm old-prefix -> new-prefix).

product-ops: For comms: recommend a short status note to affected customers and a follow-up RCA within 48h. CS, please draft.

cs-essex: Will draft now. Any numbers on affected request count?

maria: Rough: ~420k requests during 10:12-10:30 for affected prefixes, estimated 36k additional backend hits due to misses. I'll attach exact counts to RCA doc.

sachin: For the in-thread RCA work — collecting:
- full hit/miss timeline per shard (graph attached in ticket)
- list of canary buckets that received the rollout (users+traffic %)
- config diff (pre/post) for reaper/ttl
- request traces for a few 5xx examples (linked)

maria: Putting a short quick-hypothesis tracker here so we have in-thread record:
- H1 (high confidence): Prefix normalization change caused cold-miss storm. Evidence: commit + prefix_mismatch logs + recovery after pause. Confidence: high.
- H2 (medium): Eviction TTL regression exacerbated severity. Evidence: evicted_by_reaper logs + config diff. Confidence: medium.
- H3 (low): Downstream KV shard networking flaps coincidentally increased misses. Evidence: none concrete. Confidence: low.

evans: I'm uploading a few example traces and a small diff showing the prefix formatting lines. Link: https://artifacts.internal/1812345678/traces_and_diffs.zip

leah: Action items assigned:
- leah: open rewarm ticket + confirm schedule (in progress)
- sachin: assemble complete shard hit-rate graphs and attach to RCA (in progress)
- maria: prepare customer impact numbers and draft RCA narrative (in progress)
- evans: include trace samples and commit diff (done)

maria: Handoff to next oncall in 20m — summary below:
Handoff summary (10:40):
- Incident cause likely prefix normalization in PR a3f4b2 causing prefix_mismatch -> cache miss storm.
- Immediate mitigations: PR rollback paused, eviction config rolled back, +20% cache capacity, routing fallback enabled.
- Status: system recovered to baseline at 10:36. Ongoing: rewarm job (ticket RED-7892), full RCA writeup and customer comms pending.

sachin: I'll take next oncall. I'll keep monitoring hit-rate for 2 hours and validate rewarm results once scheduled.

maria: Thanks everyone. Please keep posting any stragglers or abnormal traces here. I'll start the RCA doc now and link it in this thread when ready.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1812345678 set to "Mitigated" at 10:36 UTC. Postmortem required: due 2026-03-16.

maria: RCA draft link (WIP): https://docs.internal/incidents/INC-1812345678-rca - will include full timeline, logs, root cause, and follow-ups.

sachin: Noting follow-ups for next steps:
- ensure canary rollout tooling validates cache key format before rollout (prevent schema-change rollouts without migration)
- add a canary-specific cache warm step for prefix migrations
- improve monitoring alert to correlate sudden hit-rate drops with recent rollouts automatically

cs-essex: Drafted customer note; will send after product-ops review.

maria: closing thread for active mitigation. Will reopen if any regression.

sachin: Thanks, all. We'll reconvene in RCA doc comments.
